one_liner: Rust port of simdjson with serde support; 1.2-2.7x faster DOM parsing than serde_json in json-benchmark.
what_it_does: Parses JSON bytes into a mutable DOM, a flat tape or lazy value, or any serde Deserialize type. The DOM comes in two forms: BorrowedValue, whose strings point into the input, and OwnedValue. simd_json::serde::from_slice deserializes into your serde structs (or serde_json::Value), and the crate mirrors serde_json's to_string/to_writer/from_reader names. It is not a drop-in replacement: every parse entry point takes &mut [u8] because strings are unescaped in place, from_str is unsafe and takes &mut str, and from_reader reads the whole input into memory first.
how_it_is_fast: It uses simdjson's two-stage design. Stage 1 scans 64-byte blocks with AVX2, SSE4.2, NEON or wasm simd128 byte compares, finds quoted regions with a carry-less-multiply prefix XOR (PCLMULQDQ) and odd-backslash-run detection, validates UTF-8 with simdutf8, and writes a u32 index of structural characters. Stage 2 walks that index with a goto-style state machine to build a flat tape; strings are scanned 32 bytes at a time and unescaped back into the input buffer, so BorrowedValue does not allocate per string. Floats use 8-digits-at-a-time SWAR fraction parsing, a Clinger fast path, and a 128-bit power-of-ten multiply (Eisel-Lemire style) with a std fallback, and objects use halfbrown, which stores up to 32 keys in a plain vector.
when_to_use: You parse into a generic DOM (a serde_json::Value-style tree) from byte buffers you own and may overwrite, such as request bodies or log lines. This is where json-benchmark shows 1.2-2.7x over serde_json.
The documents are string- and key-heavy (twitter.json and citm_catalog.json shapes). There, DOM parse was 1.7-2.7x and struct parse 1.7-1.9x faster than serde_json.
The workload is read-mostly and repeated: use the tape or lazy value and reuse one Buffers across calls (to_tape_with_buffers, from_slice_with_buffers) to amortize allocations.
You already have serde Deserialize types and want a faster decoder without rewriting them, on x86-64 (AVX2 or SSE4.2), aarch64 (NEON) or wasm with simd128.
You control the build and can ship a non-portable x86 binary: default-features = false plus RUSTFLAGS=-C target-cpu=native is the configuration the README says performs best.
when_not_to_use: Your input is immutable (&str, shared &[u8], read-only mmap). You must copy it into a mutable buffer first. In the 2026 tegridy-benchie run, which used to_vec plus OwnedValue, simd-json was only 1.05x serde_json at 1 thread and 1.10x at 8 threads.

The data is mostly floats (canada.json shape). Struct parse tied serde_json at 580 MB/s. In issue #370's criterion run, simd_json::serde::from_slice into serde_json::Value was slower than serde_json on canada (114 vs 153 MiB/s).
You need streaming, NDJSON, or documents of 4 GiB or more. There is no streaming parser, NDJSON is an open request (#194), and inputs of u32::MAX bytes or more return InputTooLarge.
Memory is tight. tegridy-benchie measured peak RSS of 166 MB vs 116 MB for serde_json at 1 thread, and 450 vs 379 MB at 8 threads.

You need object key order preserved past 32 keys (halfbrown switches to a hash map; #378 is open), or strict rejection of lone high-surrogate escapes (#481 is open: "\ud800" decodes to U+0000 instead of an error).

integration.dependencies: simdutf8, value-trait, halfbrown, ref-cast; serde and serde_json through the default serde_impl feature; optional beef (beef feature) and ahash (known-key feature)
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 1.88 (rust-version), edition 2024; the hints feature needs nightly
integration.platforms: x86/x86-64 with runtime dispatch to AVX2+PCLMULQDQ or SSE4.2; aarch64 (NEON); wasm32 (simd128 when enabled); a scalar fallback elsewhere that the README calls significantly slower. CI runs Linux, Windows, macOS and big-endian s390x.
integration.thread_safety: Not documented. Parsing keeps no shared mutable state apart from an atomically cached CPU-dispatch function pointer. The input and Buffers are taken by &mut, so use one Buffers per thread.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — simd_json::serde::from_slice/to_string mirror serde_json and can target serde_json::Value, but input must be &mut [u8] (from_str is unsafe and takes &mut str). The native DOM types are simd-json's own BorrowedValue/OwnedValue behind the value-trait traits, and the error types differ.

gotchas: The parser overwrites your input buffer with unescaped strings. BorrowedValue and the tape borrow from that buffer, so it must outlive them. After serde::from_str the &mut str may hold invalid UTF-8, which is why that function is unsafe.

The crate uses 'a lot' of unsafe code (README). Soundness and availability bugs were fixed recently: #471, an out-of-bounds read through an exhausted Deserializer, fixed in 0.18.1 (2026-08-23); #473, a stack overflow on deeply nested input in to_owned_value/to_borrowed_value, fixed in 0.18 with a default max depth of 1024; and #445, missing UTF-8 validation on one fallback path, merged 2026-07-08. RUSTSEC-2019-0008 (CVE-2019-15550) covered a page-boundary read in 0.1.x. Pin 0.18.1 or later.

Several behaviors depend on feature flags. Without value-no-dup-keys, duplicate keys make Value behavior unspecified. Integers wider than 64 bits fail to parse unless you enable big-int-as-float or 128bit. Enabling beef can break other crates in your dependency tree that use simd-json.

The default runtime-detection build is portable but not the fastest: the SSSE3 8-digit number path is compiled only when ssse3 is enabled at compile time. The README also recommends mimalloc, jemalloc or snmalloc over the system allocator.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Against jiter, the other Rust entry with serde_json as its baseline, pick simd-json when you need serde Deserialize structs, a mutable DOM, or serialization; jiter's README lists only JsonValue, a pull iterator and Python parsing. jiter was about 1.8x faster than simd-json in the same tegridy-benchie run (209.4 vs 115.2 MB/s at 8 threads), so prefer jiter for read-only extraction; the other siblings (go-json, Sonic, jsoniter, easyjson, Jsonifier, zzzJSON, LJSON) are Go or C/C++ and are not options in Rust.
verified_claims_summary: serde-rs/json-benchmark (2021; simd-json 0.4.11 vs serde_json 1.0.72; best of 256 trials; rustc 1.59.0-nightly with target-cpu=native and jemalloc; Intel i7-6600U) measured DOM parse 1.19x/1.71x/2.7x and struct parse 1.0x/1.72x/1.91x faster on canada/citm_catalog/twitter JSON, with DOM stringify mixed (slower on twitter, 890 vs 910 MB/s). simd-json's timer excludes its per-trial buffer copy and its BorrowedValue borrows strings that serde_json::Value owns; a 2026 real-workload run (simd-json 0.13, OwnedValue plus a copy, i7-6820HQ) showed only 1.05-1.10x.
status_note: Actively maintained (0.18.1 shipped 2026-08-23 with soundness fixes) and dual MIT OR Apache-2.0 on crates.io, but the headline numbers come from 0.4.11 in 2021 and have not been re-run independently on current versions.
